When his illness grew severe the Prophet was nursed in Aisha's house with his wives' consent and had seven skins of water poured over him before going to the people.
In his fatal illness the Prophet had Abu Bakr lead, then came out supported by Al-Abbas and Ali and sat beside him; he was nursed in Aisha's house.
In his last illness the Prophet insisted Abu Bakr lead, calling the women companions of Joseph; on Monday he lifted his curtain, smiled at the rows, and died that day.
Aisha tells how the Prophet, in his last illness, bathed and fainted repeatedly, sent Abu Bakr to lead, then prayed seated beside him while Abu Bakr and the people followed.
In his last illness the Prophet sat at Abu Bakr's left and led seated, while Abu Bakr, standing, repeated his Takbir for the people to hear.
In his last illness Aisha and Hafsa urged that Umar lead instead of the weeping Abu Bakr; the Prophet told them to keep quiet, calling them companions of Joseph.
During Fajr the Prophet lifted the curtain of Aisha's dwelling, smiled at the rows and signalled them to complete the prayer; he died late that day.
Abu Bakr kissed the dead Prophet, weeping, then told the people that whoever worshipped Muhammad, he is dead, but Allah is alive, and recited 3:144.
The Prophet died in Aisha's lap and was buried in her house, his grave not made prominent lest it be prayed at; a foot later exposed there was Umar's.
When the Prophet died, the Ansar assembled in the shed of Bani Sa'ida, and Umar and Abu Bakr went to them.
In his serious illness the Prophet, with his wives' leave, was nursed in Aisha's house, walking there supported between Al-Abbas and Ali with his feet dragging.
Weeping, Ibn Abbas recalls the Thursday the Prophet's illness worsened: people disputed his call for writing materials, and he ordered the pagans expelled from Arabia and delegates honoured.
In his last illness the Prophet is nursed in Aisha's house with his wives' leave, and dies there leaning on her chest after she softens a siwak for him.
Ibn Abbas weeps recalling Thursday, when the gravely ill Prophet asked for a scapula to write on, people disputed, and he ordered pagans expelled from Arabia and delegates given gifts.
Aisha said the Prophet died when he was sixty-three years old.
The Prophet told Fatima he would die, and she, first of his family, would follow him; Ibn Abbas read Surah 110 as foretelling it; his last address commended the Ansar.
In his last illness the Prophet feels the Khaibar poison and leads a last Maghrib; people dispute his Thursday request to write; verse 110:1 is read as foretelling his death.
Fatima weeps then laughs at his secret words; given the choice, the Prophet asks for the highest companion and uses a siwak, and Aisha recites the Mu'awwidhat over him.
Gravely ill, the Prophet curses Jews and Christians for making prophets' graves places of worship, is nursed in Aisha's house, and has Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha's objection.
Ali refuses Abbas's urging to ask the ailing Prophet about the Caliphate; the Prophet smiles at the Muslims praying Fajr, and dies in Aisha's house after using a siwak.
Abu Bakr kisses the dead Prophet, then tells the people that Muhammad is dead but Allah lives, reciting verse 3:144, and Umar collapses on hearing it.
Those who forced medicine on him are made to take it; Aisha denies he willed the rule to Ali; he left only a mule, weapons and land; Fatima grieves.
Every sick prophet is offered this world or the Hereafter; in his last illness the Prophet recited the verse on those Allah blessed, and Aisha knew he was offered it.
On his deathbed the Prophet offered to write a statement against going astray, but those present quarrelled after Umar said the Quran sufficed, and he sent them away.
During the Prophet's fatal illness Al-Abbas, foreseeing his death, urged Ali to ask him who would rule after him, but Ali refused to ask.
No prophet dies before being shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, and the Prophet's last words, his head on Aisha's thigh, were 'O Allah, the Highest Companions'.
Shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, the dying Prophet wiped his face with water, said death has stupors, and chose the highest companions with his last words.
Near his death the Prophet offered to write something to keep them from going astray; Umar said Allah's Book suffices, the people disputed noisily, and he told them to leave.
